DataLad
x: Software · since 2013 · DataLad · DataLad is ongoing work funded by NSF and German BMBF, to adapt the model of open-source software (OSS) distributions to address the technical limitations of today's data-sharing and provides a versatile data management platform. It uses software for data tracking and deployment logistics specialized for large data (git-annex) built atop Git, the most capable distributed version control system (dVCS) available today. DataLad provides access to data available from various sources (e.g. lab or consortium web-sites such as humanconnectome.org; data sharing portals such as openneuro.org and crcns.org) through a single interface. It enables students and scientists to operate on data using familiar concepts, such as files and directories, while transparently managing data access and authorization with underlying hosting providers. · 10 components · DataLad Handbook: A hands-on course in data management with DataLad, written to be worked through rather than looked up. · datalad-container: DataLad extension for working with computational containers · datalad-crawler: DataLad extension for tracking web resources as datasets · datalad-deprecated: Retired DataLad functionality, kept available · datalad-fuse: DataLad extension providing a FUSE filesystem view · datalad-installer: Installation script for DataLad and its dependencies · datalad-metalad: Next generation metadata handling for DataLad · datalad-neuroimaging: DataLad extension for neuroimaging data · datalad/git-annex: Build and distribution infrastructure that packages git-annex for DataLad's platforms. t: NeuroDebian
x: Software · since 2010 · NeuroDebian · NeuroDebian is a turnkey research software platform for all aspects of the neuroscientific research process. It takes the ideas of the software hosting portals such as NITRC on maximizing research transparency and methods sharing, one step further, by providing a comprehensive suite of readily usable and fully integrated software with a robust testing and deployment infrastructure. Consequently, it improves interoperability among the tools and frees researchers from the burden of tedious installation or upgrade procedures. That, in turn, positively affects their availability for actual research activities, as well as their motivation to test new analysis tools and stay connected with the latest methodological developments in the field. · NeuroDebian grew out of pkg-exppsy, the Debian team packaging experimental psychology software -- FSL, PyEPL, PsychoPy -- from 2005 onwards. Same people, same work, wider scope.

t: PyMVPA
x: Software · since 2009 · PyMVPA · PyMVPA is a Python-based framework for neural decoding using multivariate pattern analysis. It affords both volume- and surface-based analyses using a wide variety of supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods, representational similarity analyses, searchlight analyses, hyperalignment of representational spaces, and model-based decoding and encoding. The software also can be used for neural data other than fMRI, including analysis of MEG and EEG data through spatio-temporo-frequency band searchlights and cross-modal EEG to fMRI trans-fusion. It also has been used for analyses on data unrelated to neuroscience, demonstrating its general utility. PyMVPA also serves as a repository for sample data sets (e.g., Haxby et al. 2001) that has found wide applicability for education, development of new algorithms, or new analyses and independent research reports.

t: con/tributors
x: Software · since 2020 · con/tributors · con/tributors is a Python library and GitHub Action to automate maintenance of contributor attribution files. t: con/fscacher
x: Software · since 2020 · con/fscacher · con/fscacher is a Python library providing a persistent, file-content-aware memoization cache. Functions decorated with @cache.memoize_path are re-executed only when the fingerprint (timestamps + size) of their file arguments changes — making it easy to cache expensive operations on large file trees without stale results. It is used internally by the DANDI client and other CON tools.

t: HeuDiConv / ReproIn
x: Software · since 2015 · HeuDiConv is a flexible DICOM converter for organizing brain imaging data into structured directory layouts. As a part of the larger, NIH supported ReproNim effort, we are developing a HeuDiConv-based ReproIn solution for turnkey automatic conversion of all collected MR data to a collection of the BIDS DataLad datasets. It includes a flexible BIDS-like specification how to name scanning sequences in the scanner, and a HeuDiConv reproin.py heuristic to automate layout and conversion of the datasets. This solution is deployed at DBIC (Dartmouth Brain Imaging Center), it already facilitates reproducible research, data sharing, and uploads to central archives such as NDA.

t: DueCredit
x: Software · since 2015 · DueCredit · DueCredit provides solution for the problem of inadequate citation and referencing of scientific software and methods. It provides a simple framework (at the moment for Python only) to embed publication or other references in the original code so they are automatically collected and reported to the user at the necessary level of reference detail, i.e. only references for actually used functionality will be presented back if software provides multiple citeable implementations. · As a side-effect, we hope that DueCredit also will reduce demand in "prima-ballerina" projects, will encourage contributions to existing open-source codebases, and as a result would solidify scientific software ecosystem.

t: Initiatives
ReproNim
x: Initiatives · since 2016 · ReproNim · ReproNim: A Center for Reproducible Neuroimaging Computation. A P41 center building training, tools and standards so neuroimaging analyses can be reproduced. · 1 component · TR&D3: The technology research and development project within ReproNim that YOH leads at Dartmouth. In practice it is the tooling that makes a study reproducible end to end: capturing what the scanner and the stimulus computer actually did, converting it into standard layouts without a human in the loop, and re-running the analysis in a recorded environment. · 2 collaborative projects · DataLad: DataLad is ongoing work funded by NSF and German BMBF, to adapt the model of open-source software (OSS) distributions to address the technical limitations of today's data-sharing and provides a versatile data management platform. It uses software for data tracking and deployment logistics specialized for large data (git-annex) built atop Git, the most capable distributed version control system (dVCS) available today. DataLad provides access to data available from various sources (e.g. lab or consortium web-sites such as humanconnectome.org; data sharing portals such as openneuro.org and crcns.org) through a single interface. It enables students and scientists to operate on data using familiar concepts, such as files and directories, while transparently managing data access and authorization with underlying hosting providers. · OpenNeuro: OpenNeuro is likely the oldest and the most well known BRAIN Initiative archive for neuroimaging data. One of the exciting features of the project is that being inspired by our early DataLad crawling of its OpenfMRI.org precursor, it is now using git-annex directly as its core technology. CON is contributing in ensuring availability of recent versions of git-annex and DataLad, involved standardization efforts, and inter-archive collaborations.

t: ReproNim TR&D3
x: Initiatives · The technology research and development project within ReproNim that YOH leads at Dartmouth. In practice it is the tooling that makes a study reproducible end to end: capturing what the scanner and the stimulus computer actually did, converting it into standard layouts without a human in the loop, and re-running the analysis in a recorded environment. · 5 components · con/duct: Lightweight wrapper that records execution time, CPU and memory usage of a command, for resource-aware reproducible runs. · ReproEvents: An event relay device: a single-board microcontroller running micropython that sits between the input peripherals a participant uses and the event recording system, so button presses are timestamped by hardware rather than by whatever the stimulus computer was doing. · ReproIn: A convention and a setup for naming sequences at the scanner so that conversion to a shareable, version-controlled BIDS dataset needs no human in the loop. Runs on HeuDiConv; deployed at DBIC. · ReproMan: Tool for creating and managing reproducible computation environments and executing analyses in them. · ReproNim/containers: ReproNim/containers is a DataLad dataset providing a ready-to-use "distribution" of containerized neuroimaging environments (Singularity images) for reproducible analysis. It collects a curated set of containers — including those used by HeuDiConv and the broader ReproNim ecosystem — and exposes them via the ///repronim/containers DataLad dataset path, making it trivial to pin and share exact software environments alongside data and workflows.
